html:
The Apanyekrá are a Timbira people of Maranhão in northeastern Brazil, who speak a Gê language. With the Ramkokamekrá they are known as the Canela.

They live in round villages on the dry cerrado plains, with houses set in a ring around a central plaza. Like the Parkatêjê, they are known for log races. Cattle ranchers took much of their land from the 1700s onwards. Their neighbours include the Tupi speaking Guajajara.
